label: Scheme progress
summary: Moves a scheme's progress forward, or back with a negative amount.
details: Progress runs from 0 to 100. It works on a scheme. Vanilla mostly writes a block with a named value (`scheme_progress_gain` or `scheme_progress_loss`) and a `multiply` factor, for example `{ value = scheme_progress_gain multiply = 2 }`. Vanilla also writes a plain number or a script value directly.

fields.name: value
fields.values: a number, a script value or a named value such as scheme_progress_gain

fields.name: multiply
fields.text: Multiplies the value; a negative factor turns a gain into a loss.

fields.name: add
fields.text: Adds a further amount to the value.

fields.name: subtract
fields.text: Takes an amount off the value.

label: Secret
summary: Gives the character a new secret of the chosen type.
details: Some secret types are about another person, given as the target. Vanilla can save the new secret under a name with `save_scope_as` so later script can use it. Tooltips of effects you run on a secret in the same effect block that created it may show wrongly or not at all, because the secret does not exist yet when the tooltip is built. Running those effects later, for example in an event option, shows normally. Use custom tooltips if needed.

fields.name: type
fields.values: a secret type key, for example secret_murder

fields.name: target
fields.text: The person the secret is about, for types that need one.

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the new secret under this name for later use in the script.

label: Secret participant
summary: Adds a character as a participant of the secret.
details: It runs on a secret. The character you give is the one who becomes a participant.

label: AI short-term gold
summary: Adds gold to the short-term budget category of the character's AI budget.
details: The gold is created out of nothing. The game's text says it respects the budget's maximum and that the overflow goes to the short-term budget, which reads oddly because that is the budget being filled. Vanilla mostly gives a named gold value such as `medium_gold_value`, and once a block with `value` and `divide`.

label: Special building
summary: Builds a special building in the province.
details: Adds or changes a special building slot in the province if one is needed. The value is the key of a special building. Vanilla uses it with keys such as `hall_of_heroes_01`, `alamut_castle_02` and `generic_university`.

label: Special building slot
summary: Gives the province a slot for a special building.
details: The value names the special building the slot is for. Vanilla uses it most with `generic_university`, and also for holy site buildings and unique buildings.

label: Spread progress
summary: Adds a percentage of progress to the innovation the culture is currently spreading.
details: The amount can be a script value. It works on a culture. For example `add_spread_progress = 35` adds 35 percent.

label: Spread progress (months)
summary: Adds months of progress to the innovation the culture is currently spreading.
details: The amount is counted in months and can be a script value. It works on a culture. For example `add_spread_progress_time = 3` adds three months. The percentage version is `add_spread_progress`.

label: Stewardship perk points
summary: Gives the character perk points in the stewardship lifestyle.
details: Perk points are what the character spends to unlock perks in that lifestyle's tree. Vanilla almost always gives 1.

label: Stewardship lifestyle XP
summary: Gives the character experience in the stewardship lifestyle.
details: Vanilla mostly gives a named amount such as `minor_lifestyle_xp` or `medium_lifestyle_xp`, and sometimes a block with `value` and `multiply` to scale it.

fields.name: value
fields.values: a number, script value or named amount

label: Stewardship skill
summary: Raises the stewardship skill by an amount, or lowers it with a negative one.
details: The input does not state where it runs; going by the name it is on a character. Vanilla mostly writes a plain number such as 1 or 2, and sometimes a block with `value` or `subtract`. It also writes two numbers in braces such as `{ 3 5 }`, which looks like a range, but the game's text does not say so.

label: Stress
summary: Raises the character's stress, or lowers it with a negative amount.
details: Vanilla mostly uses named amounts such as `minor_stress_gain`, `medium_stress_loss` or `major_stress_loss`; the name says whether stress goes up or down. The amount can also be a number, a script value, or a block that calculates one.

fields.name: value
fields.values: a number, script value or named amount

label: Subject standing
summary: Changes the subject standing in the character's current subject contract.
details: It works on a character who has a subject contract. Vanilla mostly gives negative numbers (-1, -10, -20), so it lowers standing, and once a block with `value`. The game's example shows a block, `{ add = learning max = 10 }`, which suggests `max` caps the amount.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The amount, as vanilla writes it once in a block.

label: Army supply
summary: Adds supply to an army.
details: The army's supply cannot go above its maximum supply capacity. It works on an army, for example `scope:army = { add_supply = 20 }`.

label: Takeover phase duration
summary: Adds time to a coming takeover phase of a situation sub-region, or takes time away with a negative amount.
details: You name the phase and give the time in days, months or both. It works on a sub-region of a situation.

label: Takeover points
summary: Adds points towards a coming takeover phase of a situation sub-region, or removes points with a negative amount.
details: The result is rounded down. It works on a sub-region of a situation. Vanilla uses it with phases such as `investiture_crisis`, with amounts like -100 and 800.

label: Faction discontent
summary: Adds discontent to every faction that targets the character, or removes it with a negative amount.
details: It affects all factions aimed at this character at once. Vanilla gives positive numbers from 1 to 30.

label: Tenet
summary: Adds a tenet to the faith.
details: The value is the key of a tenet. It works on a faith. Vanilla uses it with keys such as `tenet_warmonger`.

label: Title law
summary: Sets a law on the title, replacing the title's current law of the same group.
details: It does not charge the cost of changing a law and does not run the law's change effects. The version that does is `add_title_law_effects`. The value is a law key such as `male_only_law`. The input does not state where it runs; the game's documentation says the title.

label: Title law (with effects)
summary: Sets a law on the title, replacing the title's current law of the same group, and applies the costs and effects of changing it.
details: The difference from `add_title_law` is that the law change costs and effects are applied. The documented example line reads `add_title_law = ...`, which looks copied from the other effect; the key itself is `add_title_law_effects`. Vanilla has no uses to check.

label: Add to activity
summary: Makes the character join the given activity as if invited and accepting.
details: The character joins with their default travel plan. The value is the activity, usually a saved scope such as `scope:activity` or `involved_activity`. The version without a travel plan is `add_to_activity_without_travel`.

label: Add to activity (no travel)
summary: Makes the character join the given activity as if invited and accepting, without giving them a travel plan.
details: The character must already be at the activity's location, otherwise they are removed from the activity. The documented example line says `add_to_activity`, which looks copied from the other effect. The value is the activity, for example `scope:activity`.

label: Agent slot
summary: Puts the character into a specific agent slot.
details: The slot is given as a value, and vanilla uses saved scopes such as `scope:agent_slot`. The game documents nothing more about agent slots.

label: Guest to a group (this phase)
summary: Adds a character to a named group of guests, in the current phase of the activity only.
details: It works on an activity. The other version, `add_to_guest_subset`, adds across phases.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character who joins the group.

label: Global variable list
summary: Adds a target to a named variable list, optionally only for a set time.
details: Going by its name, the list is a global one, kept for the whole game and not on one character or title; the game's text is the same as for the plain variable list and does not say so. Without a duration the entry stays. Vanilla uses it for lists like `unavailable_unique_decisions`, with targets such as `this`, `root` or a flag.

fields.name: target
fields.text: What is added to the list.
fields.values: a scope, such as root or scope:x, or a flag

fields.name: days
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in days.

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in weeks.

fields.name: months
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in months.

fields.name: years
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in years.

label: Guest to a group
summary: Adds a character to a named group of guests of the activity.
details: Without a phase, the character is added in all phases and in ongoing groups. With a phase, they are added in all phases of that type. Vanilla uses it for groups such as spectator, contestant and winner in tournaments. It works on an activity.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character who joins the group.

fields.name: phase
fields.text: Limits the change to phases of this type.

label: Add to list
summary: Adds the current thing to a named list, creating the list if it does not exist.
details: The list can be used later in the same unbroken event chain. If you add something permanent to a temporary list, the whole list becomes permanent. The short form is just the list name; the block form also takes a `value`. Vanilla uses the short form almost always, and the block form with flags such as `flag:favorite_destiny_character`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: A value stored with the entry.

label: Local variable list
summary: Adds a target to a named variable list, optionally only for a set time.
details: Going by its name, the list is a local one, not a global one; the game's text is the same as for the plain variable list and does not say so. Without a duration the entry stays. Vanilla has no uses to check.

fields.name: target
fields.text: What is added to the list.
fields.values: a scope, such as root or scope:x

fields.name: days
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in days.

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in weeks.

fields.name: months
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in months.

fields.name: years
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in years.

label: Add to temporary list
summary: Adds the current thing to a named temporary list, creating the list if it does not exist.
details: The list can be used later in the same effect, not beyond it. If you add a temporary target to a permanent list, the list stays permanent. The short form is just the list name; the block form also takes a `value`. Vanilla uses the short form.

fields.name: value
fields.text: A value stored with the entry.

label: Variable list
summary: Adds a target to a named variable list, optionally only for a set time.
details: Without a duration the entry stays. Vanilla uses it a lot for name lists, with `prev` or a saved scope as target. Most uses have no duration; some give years, a few days or months.

fields.name: target
fields.text: What is added to the list.
fields.values: a scope, such as prev, root or scope:x

fields.name: days
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in days.

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in weeks.

fields.name: months
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in months.

fields.name: years
fields.text: How long the entry stays, in years.

label: Trait
summary: Gives the character a trait.
details: Nothing happens, and no tooltip shows, if the character cannot have the trait: they already have it, they have an opposing trait, the trait's own condition is not met, or the character is outside the trait's allowed range. Use `add_trait_force_tooltip` to show a tooltip in those cases.

label: Trait (always shows tooltip)
summary: Gives the character a trait, and always shows a tooltip for it.
details: It adds the trait in the same cases as `add_trait`. When `add_trait` would add nothing (already has it, opposing trait, condition not met, outside the range), the tooltip is still shown but the trait is not added.

label: Trait experience
summary: Adds experience to a trait's level track on the character.
details: Name the track only if the trait has several tracks; otherwise leave it out. Vanilla uses tracks such as `foot`, `horse` and `bow`, and traits such as `tourney_participant` and `devoted`. Values are plain numbers like 10 or 20, a named value, or two numbers in braces such as `{ 20 80 }` (the game's text does not say what that means).

label: Travel option
summary: Adds a travel option to the travel plan.
details: The value is the key of the travel option. It works on a travel plan.

label: Journey modifier
summary: Adds a modifier to a travel plan.
details: The short form is just the modifier's key and has no time limit stated. The block form can set a duration in days, weeks, months or years, and an optional `desc`, a dynamic text shown for the timed modifier. Vanilla uses both forms.

fields.name: desc
fields.text: A dynamic description shown for the timed modifier.

label: Travel point of interest
summary: Adds a travel point of interest of the given type to the province.
details: Vanilla uses it with types such as `poi_grand_cathedral` and `poi_special_buildings_learning`.

label: Travel waypoint
summary: Adds a waypoint just ahead of the travel plan's current location and changes the path to pass through it.
details: The value is a province. It works on a travel plan. Vanilla uses it once, with a saved province.

label: Treasury
summary: Adds to the character's treasury.
details: The amount can be a number, a script value, or a block that calculates one. Vanilla uses a block with `value` and `min`, `max` or `multiply` to limit or scale the amount, for example `{ value = gold min = 100 }`. `add_treasury_or_gold` is the version that gives gold when the character has no treasury.

label: Treasury or gold
summary: Adds to the character's treasury if they have one, otherwise gives them gold.
details: Vanilla mostly uses named amounts such as `medium_treasury_or_gold_value`. A block with `value` and `add`, `multiply`, `min` or `max` is also used to shape the amount.

label: Truce (both ways)
summary: Creates a truce between the character and another character, binding both sides.
details: Set the length in years, months or days. A shorter new truce does not replace an existing one unless `override` is yes. `result` is the outcome seen from the character's side and is white peace if left out. Give either a casus belli or a war as the cause, not both; `name` sets a custom description and cannot be combined with a casus belli. Vanilla mostly gives the war, a length in days and a result.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The other character the truce is with.

fields.name: override
fields.text: Whether the new truce replaces an existing one even if the new one is shorter.

fields.name: result
fields.text: The outcome of the truce from the character's point of view.

fields.name: casus_belli
fields.text: The casus belli that caused the truce; cannot be combined with name or war.

fields.name: war
fields.text: The war that caused the truce; cannot be combined with casus_belli.

fields.name: name
fields.text: A custom description for the truce, with the current thing as its context.
